title: Aggregate token loss during graceful node shutdown causing under-reporting to billing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Multiple customers on Dedicated and Private deployments reported inexplicably low usage invoices for periods that included autoscale-induced machine drain events. Initial evidence shows token accounting summaries for affected nodes were truncated during graceful shutdown, resulting in under-reported tokens sent to the central billing aggregator. This ticket tracks the investigation, fix, and customer reconciliation plan.
steps_to_reproduce: Provision a small Dedicated GPU pool with autoscaling enabled (min=1, max=4).
Drive steady generation load that causes the pool to scale up to 4 nodes, then reduce load to trigger scale-down (back to 1).
During scale-down, observe node graceful shutdown sequence and watch the metering worker logs for final flush events.
Compare per-node token counters emitted to the billing pipeline vs. the runtime internal counters before shutdown.
observed_behavior: When the node receives SIGTERM for graceful drain, in-flight requests are allowed to complete but the metering worker sometimes emits a final partial flush record missing the last KV flush window.
Central aggregator accepts partial per-node reports; reconciliation job sums them and reports a lower total token count than actual generation observed by request logs.
Affected customers see under-billed invoices during the window; downstream internal audits flagged the mismatch during monthly reconciliation.
hypothesis_and_root_cause: Race between graceful-shutdown sequence and asynchronous metering flush: shutdown cancels the background batcher before the local on-disk checkpoint is atomically written.
Edge case when KV cache eviction happens concurrently with shutdown caused the metering worker to drop the last in-memory bucket instead of persisting it.
Cause only observed on Dedicated and Private nodes that exercise aggressive scale-down/autoscaling; hosted API paths have an extra acknowledgement path that prevented loss.
investigation_notes: SRE attached logs: node-id n-642f: last_flush_event emitted 2026-02-26T21:44:12Z but local request logs show tokens up to 2026-02-26T21:44:13Z (1 second drift).
Reproduction in staging succeeded with scaled-down cluster; captured a windowed trace showing metering-future canceled in shutdown handler (see trace: https://traces.redwood.ai/trace/0a3b5b).
Telemetry: 0.6% of scale-down events in the past 30 days show incomplete final flush; those events correlate with customers reporting billing anomalies.
temporary_mitigation: Disable aggressive autoscale down for impacted customer orgs (set min to current pool size) - done for orgs: cust-42, cust-77.
Enable additional logging in metering worker (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1147) and increased retention for affected buckets.
Created Datadog alert 'metering.final_flush_missed' to notify SRE when a final flush is not observed within 5s of node shutdown.
proposed_fix: Make final flush on shutdown atomic and blocking: convert background batcher to provide a synchronous drain_with_timeout(15s) API invoked by shutdown handler.
Add write-ahead log (WAL) entry for final in-flight token buckets; WAL entry acknowledged only after successful push to central aggregator.
Add idempotent ack protocol between node and billing ingest to make late replays safe (idempotency key includes node-id + epoch + bucket-range).
Backfill script to scan request logs and emit missing token deltas for windows identified as incomplete (see reconciliation plan).
rollout_plan: 1) Merge runtime and billing PRs to canary channel.
2) Deploy to staging Dedicated (canary group of 2 customers) and run synthetic scale-up/down workload for 72h.
3) After stable canary, deploy to low-traffic Dedicated pools, monitor 'final_flush_missed' and reconciliation delta.
4) Full rollout to Dedicated and Private by runtime-1.22 patch release.
5) Run backfill reconciliation for affected orgs and apply invoice adjustments where backfilled delta > $100.
qa_and_validation: Added E2E integration test that simulates SIGTERM during in-flight batched writes and verifies WAL persistence and ack path; test id: e2e-metering-042.
Manual verification: reproduce in staging and assert no 'final_flush_missed' events in 24h under stress.
Customer verification: coordinate with three impacted customers to validate that backfilled tokens match internal request logs.
communications_and_follow_up: Draft customer notification prepared and reviewed by Legal & CS (doc: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/CustomerComms/Metering) - scheduled send after successful canary.
Billing will issue credits for reconciled under-billed amounts and include a short transparency note explaining the fix.
Postmortem to be published to internal 'platform-incident' channel and later sanitized for external transparency.
